title: A memory that keeps what you tell it
description: The deep memory of a Fractera node keeps the phrases, photos, PDFs and voice notes you send to your main agent and answers «remind me about» with the date, the source and how sure it is. It runs on your own computer.
keywords: AI memory, personal memory, remember, remind me, voice notes, PDF search, search by meaning, Telegram, Claude Code, Fractera, open source

blocks.pill: OpenSource Web4 agent & app starter kit
blocks.title: A memory that keeps what you tell it
blocks.description: Say «remember» to your main agent in Telegram or in the terminal: a phrase, a photo, a PDF or a voice note. Months later ask «remind me about…», and the answer comes back with the date, the source and how sure the memory is. All of it stays on your own computer.

blocks.text: In your own words and in any language, with a photo, a document or a voice note if you like.
Understands what you mean, not a fixed word, and hands the words and the file to the memory.
Describes the file in words, turns a voice note into text, splits the phrase into facts and keeps them in your node.
The answer gathers what you said, with the date, the source and how sure it is. If it found a thing, you get its file.
While your computer has more than 1 GB free, the memory stays on. With less, your main agent turns it on for a task and off again.

head: Without it
With the deep memory
rows: Notes, photos and voice messages are scattered across apps
You send them to one bot, and the node keeps them together
Search finds only the exact words you typed
It finds things by meaning, in any language
A photo is a file without words
A photo is described in words and found by what is on it
You never know where an answer came from
Every answer names the date, the source and how sure it is
Your notes sit on someone else's server
They stay on your computer, inside your node

blocks.title: What it does with each kind of file

head: What you send
What the memory does
rows: A photo or a picture
Describes it in words and keeps the picture with the description
A PDF
Reads it whole and keeps it with a description, so you find it by what it says
A voice note
Turns it into text and reads it like any phrase
A video
Reads the frames and the sound when the computer has ffmpeg
Documents and code
Reads them as text; code is never run
A text longer than 2,000 words
Keeps it whole as one thing, without splitting it into facts

blocks.text: There are no forms to fill in and no menus to learn. You talk to your main agent the way you would talk to a person, and it knows when you mean the memory.

items: «remember…», «note down», «save this», «don't forget» — the memory keeps it.
«remind me about…», «what did I say about…» — the memory answers.
A photo, a document or a voice note with a few words — kept together and found together.
Add your OpenAI key in the core's settings. The memory uses it to search by meaning, to hear voice notes and to split phrases into facts.
Connect your main agent's Telegram bot in the core, so you can talk to it from your phone.
Say «remember…» to it. That is all.

blocks.text: Without the key the memory still keeps what you say, but it does not search by meaning and does not hear voice notes.
Any element of your node can keep things in the memory and ask it with two calls on this computer, using the node key.
The answer carries the text, the things it found, how sure it is and an `answer_id`. Your element can comment on the answer with `POST /v1/feedback`, and the full contract is at `GET /v1/contract`.

head: Part
What it does
rows: The data element
Keeps every phrase as a row in the node's database
The vectors element
Finds what you said by meaning
The graph element
Keeps the facts and their links in a space of their own
The storage element
Keeps the photos, documents and recordings
OpenAI `gpt-6-luna`
Splits a phrase into facts and describes pictures and PDFs, for a fraction of a cent
OpenAI `whisper-1`
Turns voice notes into text
Your node
Keeps the memory on while the computer has more than 1 GB free; with less, your main agent turns it on for a task
